I used to, but it doesn't get to me the same way anymore. A lot of it probably came from not having strong traditions. My family is small and most of us aren't particularly religious.

Around the time I became an adult, my mom's parents passed and the extended family suddenly wasn't making time for each other the way they used to. So I was kind of left wondering what I was supposed to do for holidays. And at some point I moved to a state I don't have family in, which means I basically spend no holidays with them.

Eventually, I started making my own traditions and finding my own ways to celebrate and send cheer to my family.

It sort of started with seasonal craft beers. I lived in a place for a while where the local breweries made Christmas beers, like with the flavors of eggnog or ginger snaps. It awoke a whimsical creative spirit in me that persists to this day, even though I can't get them where I am now. Maybe someday I'll learn to brew and make them.

Once that instinct was awoken in me, I suddenly instinctively connected with holidays and started feeling inspired by them to decorate and reach out to family.

I tend to take things they've done with me as my own traditions and then share that with them to feel connected across the miles. For instance, most of my holiday recipes come from my sister, and today I went out shooting because I used to go with my parents on holidays.
